clue.text: Growth of Percy's todger

indicators.note: 'growth of' these words says the answer is grown inside them, spanning the break between two words

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about the size of a man named Percy's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Percy's todger' looks like the thing growing; the letters run across the possessive into the next word. A todger is British slang for a penis.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac-like swelling, one kind of abnormal growth in the body.

clue.text: Males after booze, say, as joke ends?

indicators.note: 'say' makes booze stand for its sound-alike boos, a plural, so the jeer-plus-male unit occurs twice
'after' puts each male behind a jeer

parts.note: booze sounds like boos, jeers of disapproval
M is the abbreviation for male; the plural gives one for each jeer

explanation.surface: Men turning up after the drinking, as a story's punchline arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booze, say' sounds like 'boos', so there are two jeers (BOO, BOO), and 'Males' supplies an M after each. Boom boom! is the catchphrase of Basil Brush, a British puppet fox who says it after every joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry marks a punchline, much as a drum roll and cymbal close a comedian's gag, so it comes where gags finish.

clue.text: Journalist keeps cutting of very small one of the 20A

indicators.note: 'keeps' says the journalist holds the next piece inside

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

indicators.note: 'cutting of' trims the tail off the word for very small

parts.note: dwarf as an adjective means very small, undersized

explanation.surface: A reporter retaining clippings about a tiny member of some group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting of' trims the final F. 20A is FOXES: Edward Fox is the English actor of The Day of the Jackal.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Edward Fox belongs to the Fox acting family, so he is one of a set of people surnamed Fox.

clue.text: Wrong about current place for headpiece?

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
C, for circa, means about
I is the physics symbol for electric current
to put is to place

explanation.surface: Something went wrong with where a hat or helmet is meant to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'headpiece' means a piece of the head, not a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinciput is the front upper part of the skull, literally a part of the head, so a punning headpiece.

clue.text: Ranking data about university

indicators.note: 'about' says the data goes round the next piece

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are data

explanation.surface: League-table figures about how a university ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or position relative to others, which is what a ranking measures.

clue.text: Narrow ways unknown in Norfolk area

indicators.note: 'in' puts the unknown inside the Norfolk area

parts.note: the Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in Norfolk, England
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: Little-known lanes in a corner of Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a waterway district in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Byroads are minor side roads, the narrow lanes off the main routes.

clue.text: Girl's cologne knocked over? Bother!

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: something knocked over lies the other way round, so the scent's name is turned back

parts.note: Brut is a well-known brand of men's cologne

explanation.surface: Someone tipped over a girl's perfume bottle, and she exclaims in annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns BRUT into TURB. 'Bother!' looks like an exclamation but is the imperative verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to bother or interrupt them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Regularly endure erectile dysfunction when eating a bit of Stilton cheese

indicators.note: 'eating' says the shuffled letters take in the next piece
a dysfunction is a failure to work properly, so the letters are thrown into disorder
'Regularly' takes every other letter of the word endure

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: 'a bit of' takes only the opening letter of the cheese named

explanation.surface: A man copes with impotence while snacking on Stilton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dysfunction' looks like part of the medical phrase but signals the anagram, giving RED LEICETER before the S goes in. Red Leicester and Stilton are English cheeses.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Leicester is a hard orange English cow's-milk cheese, a type of the general food.

clue.text: Smallest bit of a cat, found in first half of dictionary?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A tiny piece of a cat, of the kind looked up early in a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue is a second hint: words from A to M fill the first half of a dictionary, so the answer reads A TO M as well as A TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom was long thought the smallest indivisible particle of matter, hence the tiniest possible bit.

clue.text: Dispensed cold tea, drunk by nearly everybody

indicators.note: 'by' places the shuffled tea beside the shortened word
'nearly' drops the final letter of the word for everybody

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cold tea was served out and nearly everyone drank it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ALL to AL; 'drunk' rearranges COLD TEA as LOCATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Allocated means handed out or apportioned, the same as dispensed in its sense of distributing.

clue.text: See 8
Keen to eat duck? Duck it is then!

indicators.note: 'to eat' says the eager word swallows the next piece

parts.note: avid means keen, eager
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone eager to eat duck is then told to dodge it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'duck' is O, from cricket's nought; the second is the verb meaning to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or sidestep it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Aromatic substance briefly added to a jelly

indicators.note: 'added to' joins the shortened piece onto the single letter
'briefly' clips the final letter of the word

parts.note: spice is an aromatic flavouring substance

explanation.surface: A dash of seasoning stirred into a jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts SPICE to SPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Quack doctor holding job in Iran

indicators.note: 'in' puts the doctor-and-job unit inside the country's code

parts.note: IR is the international vehicle code for Iran

indicators.note: 'holding' says the doctor's letters wrap round the word for job

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A fake medic has landed a position in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quack' looks like the doctor's adjective but is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack is a fraud pretending to medical skill, and an impostor is anyone passing as someone they are not.

clue.text: Love writer's fluid approach to last of Miss Piggy's comments

indicators.note: 'approach to' brings the final piece up next

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, so O
ink is the fluid a writer uses

indicators.note: 'last of' takes the end letter of the word

explanation.surface: A writer's flowing account of what Miss Piggy of the Muppets ends up saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Piggy' reads as one name, but Miss gives its last letter and 'Piggy's comments' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinks are the grunting noises pigs make, so they are what a piggy would say.

clue.text: One of the 20A keeping quiet in Python sketch

indicators.note: 'keeping' says the name holds the next letter inside

parts.note: 20A is FOXES; Sam Fox is the British singer and former model Samantha Fox
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A member of some group stays silent during a comedy sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Samantha Fox was a 1980s British pop singer and model.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a famous Monty Python sketch set in a café where every dish comes with tinned meat.

clue.text: Quick! Run away before trouble starts

indicators.note: 'before' puts the escape ahead of the next letter

parts.note: to flee is to run away

indicators.note: 'starts' takes the opening letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: An urgent warning to get away before things turn nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift or nimble, so it is an adjective synonym of quick.

clue.text: Accommodating mischief maker turning up at 11 before light entertainment starts

indicators.note: 'at' joins the next piece straight on
in a down clue turning up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: an elf is a mischievous sprite
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

indicators.note: 'starts' takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A cheerful prankster arrives at eleven, just before the comedy show begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses ELF to FLE. '11' looks like a reference to 11-down but is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flexible bends to fit others' needs, which is what being accommodating means.

clue.text: Some numbered houses where choice is offered

indicators.note: 'houses' says the two words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Several numbered houses where residents get to pick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun after 'numbered' but is the containment verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes a diner may pick from, so it is where choices are laid out.

clue.text: Diverse assortment of GB athletes originally?

indicators.note: 'originally' says only the opening letter of athletes joins the two letters for Britain

parts.note: GB, Great Britain, plus the first letter of athletes is what the answer's jumbled second word gives

explanation.surface: A varied collection of British athletes, as they first lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, shuffle the word BAG, and you get GB plus A, the opening of 'athletes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed bag is an idiom for a varied collection of things of differing kinds and quality.

clue.text: Reserve page for feature on Antarctica?

parts.note: ice means coolness or reserve of manner
a sheet is a page of paper

explanation.surface: Booking a page in a publication for an article on Antarctica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' reads as a magazine article, but it means a landscape feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent is covered by a vast ice sheet, its defining geographical feature.

clue.text: Coins as part of wages

parts.note: the clue describes coins of a pale metal handed over in a pay packet

explanation.walkthrough: Pay used to come partly in coins of this metal, and it is also the colour of a silver fox, in keeping with the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is the collective name for coins of that colour, the small change once found in a pay packet.

clue.text: Those against us penning Times puzzles

indicators.note: 'penning' says the enemies enclose the next letter like a pen

parts.note: foes are those against us, enemies
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Enemies writing the Times crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times puzzles' suggests the newspaper's crosswords; Times is the X and 'puzzles' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to baffle them, so the verb form puzzles fits it exactly.

clue.text: Rushed fellow telling story

parts.note: telling a story, a fib, is lying

explanation.surface: A man in a hurry spinning a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying means going very fast, so rushed in the sense of hurried.

clue.text: Veteran that is rated top in cunning, like a good fighter

indicators.note: 'in' puts the run of pieces inside the word for cunning

parts.note: sly means cunning
old means veteran, long-serving
ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: 'top' takes the first letter of the word rated

explanation.surface: An old hand, considered top for craftiness, has the makings of a fine warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldierly means having the qualities of a good soldier: disciplined, brave, smart.

clue.text: First of Michael and Megan to be missing from 15 in Bath?

indicators.note: 'to be missing from' takes a letter away from the earlier answer

parts.note: 15-across is SPAM

indicators.note: 'First of' takes the opening letter of the pair of names, which both begin with the same letter

explanation.surface: Two people named Michael and Megan absent from a Python sketch in the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and Megan' adds nothing but surface: both names start with the same letter. Bath is an English city famous for its Roman hot springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is the classic example of a spa town, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Party to Civil Service IT files?

indicators.note: 'to' simply joins the two pieces

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Attending a Civil Service party about its computer systems.
explanation.definitionFit: Docs is short for documents, the files stored on a computer.

clue.text: Team of tummy ticklers heading north

indicators.note: heading north says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A group of people who tickle bellies, setting off northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'heading north' reads the letters upward, so YTIC from the two words becomes the answer. 'of' is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: City is a common short name for football clubs such as Manchester City or Leicester City.

clue.text: Thin layer of honey eaten by Teletubby, say

indicators.note: 'eaten by' says the honey goes inside the next piece
'say' signals a spelling by sound rather than the written name

parts.note: Laa-Laa is the yellow Teletubby in the children's TV show
mel is Latin for honey, found in crossword use

explanation.surface: A thin smear of honey gobbled by a children's TV character.
explanation.walkthrough: Laa-Laa is the yellow Teletubby; 'say' respells the name as LALA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamella is a thin plate or layer, as in gills or bone, a technical synonym.

clue.text: Find United at new home for the 20A

indicators.note: 'at' joins the last piece on

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names
a fox's den is called an earth

explanation.surface: Discovering a football club housed at a new den for foxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth means to dig up or discover, a direct synonym of find.
